name: Japanese Pilsner
description: A crisp, highly carbonated light lager -- the standard ramen-shop beer order in Japan.

name: Junmai Sake (Dry)
description: A dry, umami-forward sake with little sweetness to compete with the broth.

name: Whisky Highball
description: Whisky and soda over ice -- light, carbonated, and a common izakaya companion to rich food.

name: Umeshu (Plum Wine)
description: A sweet-tart fermented plum liqueur, often served on the rocks.

name: Shochu Highball
description: Barley or sweet-potato shochu cut with soda -- lighter and less smoky than whisky.

name: Japanese IPA
description: A hoppy, bitter craft beer, increasingly common alongside richer modern ramen shops.

name: Nigori Sake (Unfiltered)
description: A cloudy, lightly sweet unfiltered sake with a soft, rice-forward finish.

name: Hoppy (Beer-Flavored Soda + Shochu)
description: A low-malt beer-flavored soda mixed with shochu -- an izakaya staple built for pairing with heavy food.

name: Iced Barley Tea (Mugicha)
description: A roasted, caffeine-free barley tea served cold -- a traditional, palate-resetting default.

name: Ramune (Japanese Soda)
description: A sweet, highly carbonated soda in its signature marble bottle.

name: Hot Green Tea
description: A grassy, savory-adjacent hot tea that echoes umami rather than cutting through fat.

name: Yuzu Soda
description: A bright, citrus-forward carbonated soda -- a sharper non-alcoholic cutting option.

name: Cold Roasted Oolong Tea
description: A roasted, slightly smoky iced tea often served free at ramen counters.

name: Calpis (Calpico)
description: A sweet, lightly tangy cultured milk soft drink, usually served over ice.

name: Gyoza (Pan-Fried Dumplings)
description: Pork-and-garlic dumplings, crisp on one side -- ramen-shop's most common side order.

name: Age Gyoza (Deep-Fried Dumplings)
description: The same pork-and-garlic filling, deep-fried whole for a crackling shell.

name: Karaage (Fried Chicken)
description: Bite-sized marinated fried chicken -- savory and rich enough to match a hearty bowl.

name: Hiyayakko (Cold Tofu)
description: Chilled silken tofu with scallion and shoyu -- a light, cooling contrast to a rich bowl.

name: Chahan (Fried Rice)
description: Wok-fried rice with egg and scallion -- a classic ramen-shop combo-set companion.

name: Edamame
description: Salted, steamed soybeans in the pod -- a light, low-effort starter.

name: Chicken Skewers (Yakitori)
description: Grilled chicken skewers glazed in a sweet-savory tare.

name: Pickled Vegetables (Tsukemono)
description: A small dish of assorted pickles -- sharp, salty, and fermented.

name: Rayu (Chili Oil)
description: A spicy, toasted chili oil spooned in at the table to add heat and aroma.

name: Raw Minced Garlic
description: A small dish of raw minced garlic, common at Kyushu tonkotsu counters.

name: Black Vinegar (Kurozu)
description: A splash of mellow black vinegar, a real Kyushu tradition for cutting a heavy tonkotsu broth.

name: Toasted Sesame Seeds
description: A spoonable jar of toasted sesame, ground fresh at the table.

name: Shichimi Togarashi (Seven Spice)
description: A citrus-and-chili spice blend shaken over the bowl for a sharp, aromatic heat.

name: Extra Menma
description: A side portion of fermented bamboo shoots for anyone who wants more.

name: White Pepper
description: A sharper, more floral heat than black pepper, common on Kyushu counters.

name: Rice Vinegar (Su)
description: A plain, mellow rice vinegar splashed in to brighten and cut a heavy bowl.

name: Extra Nori
description: An additional sheet of dried seaweed, dipped rather than left to soak.

name: Yuzu Kosho
description: A fermented citrus-and-chili paste, adding brightness and heat in a very small dose.

name: Grated Ginger
description: Freshly grated ginger stirred in for a sharp, warming lift.

name: A Squeeze of Lime
description: A modern touch some shops offer to brighten a rich bowl at the very end.

name: Chili Threads (Fresh Red Chili)
description: Thin sliced fresh chili scattered on top for color, aroma, and a cleaner heat than oil.

name: Matcha Soft Serve
description: A cold, bittersweet matcha soft serve -- a temperature and sweetness contrast rather than a flavor bridge.

name: Anmitsu
description: Chilled agar jelly with fruit and syrup -- light, cool, and cleansing after a rich bowl.

name: Mochi Ice Cream
description: Small chewy rice-dough shells wrapped around ice cream -- a light, sweet finish.

name: Warabimochi (Bracken Starch Mochi)
description: Soft, jelly-like mochi dusted in roasted soybean flour -- mild and only lightly sweet.

name: Black Sesame Pudding
description: A silky, nutty pudding that echoes a bowl's own toasted sesame or garlic notes.
